question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

To win laurels
solution:
The correct answer is: **To achieve honours and glory'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

__
 
• The idiom '**to win laurels**' means to achieve honours and glory through one's accomplishments. (अपनी उपलब्धियों के माध्यम से सम्मान और गौरव प्राप्त करना)

 
 
• **For example-** *Anand is a very hard-working boy, he is sure to win laurels in life.*
 
 
 
• The word '**laurels**' refers to a wreath made of leaves, traditionally given as a symbol of victory or honour.
 
• This idiom is often used in the context of sports, competitions, or academic achievements.
 
 
• **Example**: *After winning the gold medal at the Olympics, the athlete had finally won the laurels she had been striving for.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Option 2: '**To be fooled by others**' - This is not the correct meaning of the idiom. It is an unrelated meaning.
 
• Option 3: '**To win an easy battle**' - This is not the correct meaning of the idiom. It implies that the victory was too easy and not necessarily deserving of laurels.
 
• Option 4: '**To secure a well-paying job**' - This is not the correct meaning of the idiom. It is an unrelated meaning.
